subject: economics
title: Protectionism
welcome_lead: Tariffs, quotas and dumping - when politics blocks trade.
meta_desc: A-Level Trade: tariffs, quotas, subsidies, dumping.
final_note: Protection helps domestic producers but usually harms consumers more.

concepts.def: Selling exports below cost or below home price.
Justification for temporary protection of new industries.

walkthroughs.body_html: A tariff raises import prices, shifting demand to domestic producers. Government earns revenue, consumers pay more, and deadweight loss arises.
A quota caps quantity rather than raising price. Foreign producers (or licence holders) capture the rents that would otherwise go to the government as tariff revenue.
Common arguments include infant industries, strategic sectors, employment and anti-dumping. Each is plausible in theory but is often abused as cover for politically connected industries.

options: Selling exports below cost or below home price
